findings.title: Shared levels are uploaded and downloaded over unauthenticated HTTP
findings.code_excerpt:
public final static String USERLEVELS_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoMonoMirror4k/get_level.php";
public final static String USERLEVELS_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoMonoMirror4k/save_level.php";
findings.entry_point: User-created levels originate in game/ApoMonoEditor.java:153-155. Downloaded, attacker-controlled response bytes enter through userlevels/ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.java:181-184.
findings.sink: URLConnection sends and receives level data at userlevels/ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.java:122-138 and 164-184 using the HTTP URLs at ApoMonoConstants.java:7-8.
findings.data_path: ApoMonoPanel.java:87-89 starts loadUserlevels(); ApoMonoPanel.java:367-374 creates the worker thread; ApoMonoUserlevels.java:22-30 calls ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.load() and publishes the returned strings as ApoMonoLevel.editorLevels. Uploads follow ApoMonoEditor.uploadString() at lines 153-157 through ApoMonoUserlevels.addLevel() at lines 85-91 to ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.save().
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker controlling the server or an on-path Wi-Fi, proxy, DNS, or routing position intercepts the plaintext POST. They replace the get_level.php body with their own syntactically valid level record, which the client installs in editorLevels, or alter an uploaded level before it reaches save_level.php. This gives the attacker control over shared-level integrity and can feed the parser in finding ApoMonoAndroid-03.
findings.preconditions: ApoMonoActivity.isOnline() must return true as implemented at ApoMonoActivity.java:69-73; the packaged application must have INTERNET permission and permit cleartext traffic; the attacker must control the endpoint or network path.
findings.validation_plan: Run the app or a source-compatible harness through an intercepting HTTP proxy. If the historical host is unavailable, transparently route www.apo-games.de:80 to a local stub. Observe the plaintext Get= POST, return one valid 11-line record, and confirm ApoMonoLevel.editorLevels is populated and the user-level button becomes visible. Upload an editor level and confirm the proxy can read and change the level= form body without any TLS failure.

findings.title: Unbounded level-server response can exhaust heap and CPU
findings.entry_point: A malicious server or plaintext-network attacker controls the response stream returned by urlConn.getInputStream() at ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.java:181.
findings.sink: The EOF-terminated loop at ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.java:184-209 appends every response line to unbounded ArrayLists. After EOF, ApoMonoUserlevels.java:61-75 performs insertion-style sorting with a nested loop over all accepted levels.
findings.data_path: ApoMonoPanel.init() automatically calls loadUserlevels() at ApoMonoPanel.java:87-89; its worker at lines 367-374 calls ApoMonoUserlevels.loadUserlevels(), then ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.load(), readLine(), the ArrayList add operations, and sortByUpload(). No user selection is required.
findings.attack_scenario: The attacker serves hundreds of thousands of complete 11-line records or keeps sending records without EOF. The loader retains every line in eleven growing lists; if the body eventually ends, the quadratic sort adds sustained CPU use. The attacker gains a remotely triggered application hang or OutOfMemoryError/process termination.
findings.preconditions: The same network and cleartext preconditions as ApoMonoAndroid-01 apply. The attacker must keep the HTTP connection open or supply a sufficiently large response.
findings.validation_plan: Route get_level.php to a controlled HTTP stub. Repeatedly emit an 11-line record consisting of level 000, numeric values for the float/integer slots, and a short name, either indefinitely or for several hundred thousand records. Launch the online app and monitor adb shell dumpsys meminfo plus logcat. Monotonic heap growth, prolonged sorting after EOF, an OutOfMemoryError, or process death confirms the finding.

findings.title: Downloaded level strings reach fixed-position parsing without format validation
findings.entry_point: The first line of every network record is accepted as a level at ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.java:184-186.
findings.sink: ApoMonoPuzzleGame.loadLevel() performs unchecked substring conversion at lines 240-242 and unchecked l.charAt(cur) access at line 248.
findings.data_path: ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.load() stores the network line; ApoMonoUserlevels.sortByUpload() checks only s.length() > 2 at lines 61-64; getAllLevelsSorted() publishes it at lines 44-56. A tap on the user-level menu invokes ApoMonoMenu.java:59-60, ApoMonoPanel.setGame() at lines 249-262, and ApoMonoPuzzleGame.loadLevel(), where fixed-position parsing occurs.
findings.attack_scenario: The attacker returns a complete 11-line server record whose level line is x00 and whose remaining numeric fields are valid. The record passes the length check and makes the user-level menu available. When the player selects it, Integer.valueOf("x") throws NumberFormatException on line 240. A three-digit numeric level such as 000 instead reaches charAt(3) at line 248 and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The attacker gains a repeatable client crash after one menu action.
findings.preconditions: The attacker must control the level-server response through server compromise or the plaintext channel, provide all eleven metadata lines so sorting succeeds, and the player must tap the downloaded user-level entry.
findings.validation_plan: Serve one record with lines: x00, 1, 1, 1, name, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1. Launch the app online, wait for the user-level button, tap it, and capture logcat. A NumberFormatException whose stack reaches ApoMonoPuzzleGame.java:240 proves the path. Repeat with level 000 to confirm StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at line 248.

findings.title: Tampered solved-level preference directly controls progression gates
findings.entry_point: The locally stored SharedPreferences value named solvedLevels is read at game/ApoMonoPanel.java:134-135. The preference store is created at ApoMonoActivity.java:37.
findings.sink: ApoMonoLevelChooser.java:64 copies ApoMonoPanel.getMaxCanChoosen() into canStart, and lines 83-84 use canStart as the gate for starting a level.
findings.data_path: ApoMonoPanel.loadPreferences() reads the string and calls ApoMonoSave.createArrayFromString(); ApoMonoSave.java:30-34 increments solvedCout for every token, including duplicates; ApoMonoPanel.java:395-400 computes the unlocked limit as solvedCout + 2; ApoMonoLevelChooser.java:83-84 trusts that value.
findings.attack_scenario: A local user with access to app-private data edits ApoMonoPref.xml and replaces solvedLevels with many repeated valid entries such as 0,0,0,... . On restart, each duplicate increments solvedCout even though only array element zero is set. The resulting count is capped only at the game's maximum and unlocks later levels without solving them. The gain is cheating in the local progression system, not privilege outside the game.
findings.preconditions: The user needs app-data access, such as a rooted device, debug/emulator build with run-as or Device Explorer access, or a writable/restorable application-data backup. Stock unrooted release-app sandboxing would normally prevent direct XML editing.
findings.validation_plan: On a debug emulator, stop the app and use run-as or Android Studio Device Explorer to set the ApoMonoPref shared-preference string solvedLevels to at least one hundred comma-separated zeroes. Restart, open the normal level chooser, and verify that levels far beyond the legitimate progress point can be selected. Inspect solvedCout or getMaxCanChoosen() to confirm that duplicate tokens, rather than distinct solved levels, produced the unlock.

notes: Coverage is 66 distinct Java contents: 26 application/generated files and 40 bundled-library files; the second 38-file MIDI tree and second 2-file andmodplug tree are exact duplicates and were deduplicated. This extraction contains no AndroidManifest.xml or build configuration, so INTERNET permission, target SDK, backup policy, and Android cleartext policy cannot be verified. A fixed native load exists in _from_jar_andmodplug-1.0/com/peculiargames/andmodplug/PlayerThread.java:910-913, and the bundled MIDI API accepts File/InputStream at _from_jar_android-midi-libv3/com/leff/midi/MidiFile.java:60-76, but no application-source class imports or calls either library; the actual music path uses packaged resource IDs with MediaPlayer at ApoMonoMusicPlayer.java:42-57. Those native/file-parser paths are therefore theoretical and unreachable in this variant and were not reported as findings. No defineClass/custom ClassLoader, ObjectInputStream, MessageDigest, applet entry point, user.home/user.dir path construction, highscore endpoint, or replay-format parser appears in the reviewed source.
